raw_response:
My land has been growing wheat and corn for as long as I can remember. My father grew wheat and corn. I grow wheat and corn. That's what this land is good for, and that's what the village buys and sells. I have about 8 mu total — the same fields I've worked for over 40 years.

Winter wheat goes in every October and comes off in June. Then I turn around and put corn in on the same fields. I do this every year. I don't need to think about it.

For wheat, I'll put down base fertilizer when I till — compound fertilizer plus some urea. Then top-dress in spring when the plants start to grow again. I flood irrigate four times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots, again in March when it greens up, at jointing, and at heading. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once for disease and aphids near heading. I use the same wheat variety the seed shop in town sells, the one most people in the village buy. I get around 400 jin per mu most years, sometimes more.

For corn, right after I cut the wheat, I plant corn directly — no time to waste. I use hybrid seed, the kind that comes in the small bags with the company name. I apply fertilizer at planting and top-dress when the corn is knee-high. I only irrigate if there's no rain by the time it tassels. Corn mostly gets the summer rains. Harvest in September.

I'm 65 and my back isn't what it was. My son sends money from the city. I'll manage these 8 mu myself, same as every year.
